items.headline: Sensex rebounds 879 points to 72,472.33 and Nifty 1.3% to 22,520.45 as oil eases; IT index up 3%
items.summary: Recovers most of Thursday's 1,045-point slump. FMCG rose about 2.2%; 2,344 stocks rose and 1,686 fell. Cooler crude and bond yields helped after the US said it would not strike Iran before the midterms. Reversing.
items.rationale: A pause in the oil spike eases the main pressure on Indian stocks; exporters gain from the weak rupee, but the rebound rests on a fragile geopolitical pledge.

items.headline: Foreign investors sell ₹3,569 crore, down from ₹12,944 crore; domestic funds buy ₹4,743 crore
items.summary: A sixth straight day of foreign selling, but the pace fell by about three-quarters, and domestic buying more than absorbed it. Figures are provisional. Easing.
items.rationale: Slower foreign selling lightens pressure on index heavyweights and the rupee; the streak itself shows foreign money is still leaving.

items.headline: Forex reserves fall $12.95 billion to $734.61 billion, a fourth weekly drop
items.summary: In the week to 2 October, foreign currency assets fell $10.66 billion and gold $2.29 billion. Reserves are down $51.1 billion from the record $785.7 billion in early September as the RBI sells dollars to defend the rupee. Escalating.
items.rationale: Fast-falling reserves show heavy rupee defence; they remain large, but the pace limits how long the RBI can lean against oil-driven dollar demand.

items.headline: RBI opens a special dollar window for three state-run fuel retailers from 12 October
items.summary: The RBI will sell dollars through designated banks to cover their full daily needs, until further notice. It also cut the threshold for FX derivatives without underlying exposure to $5 million from $100 million and barred rebooking. The rupee is near its record low. New.
items.rationale: Taking the biggest oil-import dollar buyers out of the market eases pressure on the rupee and curbs speculation, but it draws further on reserves.

industries.why: Steady dollar supply for fuel retailers

items.headline: 10-year G-Sec yield eases to about 7.28% from 7.29% as oil cools
items.summary: A one-basis-point dip after Thursday's jump to the highest close in almost three years. Still up from 7.19% before the RBI hike. Pausing.
items.rationale: A pause in yields gives borrowers brief relief, but levels stay near three-year highs while oil and rate-hike risks persist.

items.headline: US says it will not strike Iran before 3 November midterms; Brent slips 1.6% to about $102.60
items.summary: The US cited 'productive discussions' with Tehran but kept its blockade of Iranian ports. Brent had jumped above $105 on reports of strike plans. Easing, but fragile.
items.rationale: Less risk of a new strike trims the oil risk premium, easing India's import bill and inflation; ongoing tanker attacks limit how far crude can fall.

items.headline: Hormuz tanker attacks hit a wartime high; strait shipping falls 36% as US sanctions 17 Iranian vessels
items.summary: Iran is trying to choke off rivals' oil exports while the US tightens sanctions on Iran's fleet. Follows a record weekly level of attacks last week. Escalating.
items.rationale: Falling Hormuz traffic tightens supply of the crude and LNG India relies on, keeping freight, insurance and delivered prices high despite the strike pledge.

items.headline: Red Sea war-risk insurance rises after Houthi blockade; three Saudi crude tankers turn back
items.summary: The tankers made U-turns after a Houthi warning, and insurers raised rates, sources say. The Red Sea is the main alternative route for Gulf crude avoiding Hormuz. New escalation.
items.rationale: Closing the Red Sea bypass would leave Gulf crude bound for India with fewer safe routes, pushing up freight costs and Indian exporters' shipping bills to Europe.

items.headline: India faces a Qatar LNG supply cut after an Iran strike; LPG imports shift to UAE as US supply falls 58%
items.summary: Gas buyers are scrambling for other cargoes; Oman led India's LNG imports in September. Ongoing supply squeeze since the Gulf war began.
items.rationale: Less Qatari LNG raises spot gas costs for fertiliser plants, city gas and power, while LPG sourcing shifts keep cooking gas subsidies under pressure.
